units.title: Parts of speech and sentences
units.intro: A sentence needs a subject and a finite verb. Know the parts of speech before you write.

cards.title: Sentence check
body: Every full sentence has a subject and a finite verb. 'Opening the door' is not a sentence.

why: It has a subject and a finite verb.

units.title: Reading for the main idea
units.intro: The main idea is what the whole text is about, not one detail.

cards.title: How to find it
body: Read the title and the first sentence of each paragraph.
Ask: what is this text mostly about?
A detail is one example. The main idea covers the whole text.

cards.title: A short text
paras: Students in Keren meet after class to revise grammar.
They write one sentence each and correct a partner's mistake.
They say the group helps them remember more than reading alone.

questions.a: Revising together helps the students remember.

questions.q: The main idea of the Keren text is
why: The last sentence states the point of the text.

units.title: Writing a paragraph
units.intro: A paragraph has a topic sentence, supporting sentences, and a closing sentence.

cards.title: Paragraph parts
head: Part
Job
rows: names the subject and the controlling idea
restates the point without copying the first sentence

cards.title: Topic sentence
cards.problem: Which is the better topic sentence about saving water in Asmara?

steps.text: Water is wet. This names no idea.
Families in Asmara can save water in three simple ways. This names the subject and the idea.

cards.answer: Families in Asmara can save water in three simple ways.

options.C: Families in Asmara can save water in three simple ways.

why: It names the subject and the controlling idea.
